summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and cardiomyopathy was admitted for acute shortness of breath and orthopnea. She had progressive dyspnea over a week, a mild cough, and was unable to lie flat. Initial evaluation revealed moderate pulmonary edema on chest X-ray and elevated blood pressure. She was treated with BiPAP, nitroglycerin drip, and underwent hemodialysis with removal of 2.3 liters of fluid, leading to significant improvement in respiratory status. A repeat X-ray showed reduced opacities, though a retrocardiac infiltrate raised concern for possible pneumonia, prompting a course of levofloxacin. Echocardiogram confirmed severe diastolic dysfunction and moderate pulmonary hypertension, unchanged from prior. Her blood pressure stabilized, allowing discontinuation of the nitro drip and resumption of oral antihypertensives. She was discharged home breathing room air, with instructions to restrict fluids, continue antibiotics, and hold cinacalcet until after her next dialysis session.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Chronic glomerulonephritis in diseases classified elsewhere
